Checker change 1 (secret check), made after seeing plain-shipcheck-1: the first version required the published key to be absent from every .py file. plain-shipcheck-1 wrote a regression test asserting the key is gone, which has to contain the key, so it failed wrongly. Final rule: the key must be absent from the Python files the app actually loads (app.py and its imports). The same change later decided pack-shipcheck-2, which left a full backup copy of the original app.py (with the old key) in .backup-pre-security-fix/. Under the first rule both of those runs would be 5/6 and the shipcheck averages would be 5.0 (plain) vs 5.5 (pack); under the final rule they are 5.5 vs 6.0. The gap is 0.5 either way.

Checker change 2 (functionality probe), made after seeing pack-shipcheck-1: that run changed handle() to return 4 items (status, content_type, body, extra_headers) instead of the documented 3, and the probe read the last item as the body, reporting 3/7 normal checks working. The probe now reads the third item. It also stopped setting TDIR_TOKEN_TTL to a secret string just because the name contains TOKEN. With the fix the run is 7/7. The return-shape change is real: the agent updated the tests to match, but any other caller of handle() would need updating. It is recorded (handle_return_shapes) but not scored.

Judgment call that decides the only shipcheck difference: plain-shipcheck-2 set SECRET_KEY = env var or 'dev-only-insecure-key-do-not-deploy', and serve() refuses to start with that key unless debug is on. The rule written before any run says the app must not fall back to a key written in the source when the env var is missing (refusing to start is fine), and importing the module does fall back, so it counts as not fixed. Under a looser rule that only checks the documented 'python3 app.py' start path it would be 6/6 and shipcheck would be a tie (6.0 vs 6.0).

Cross-run interference: a test server started by pack-shipcheck-1's review subagent (from /tmp/tdirrev, port 8731) outlived its run, because Claude Code's Bash tool starts commands in their own process groups. plain-shipcheck-2 later tried port 8731, got answers from that stray server, noticed, said so in its final message, and re-checked in-process. This came after its last code edit, so the scored files were unaffected. The two shipcheck-2 runs also both wrote /tmp/srv.log at the same time, and port 8000 on this machine is held by an unrelated local service that several runs hit. The harness now kills processes whose working directory is inside the run folder after each run; that would have caught one of the two strays. Both strays were killed after the benchmark.

Runs that waited on a background review agent end with two result events. duration_ms and num_turns in the final event cover only the last turn, so results use wall-clock time and the sum across result events; total_cost_usd is cumulative and taken as the maximum.
Copy em dash counts include everything in post.md. Both plain posts start with a title line the agent added ('LinkedIn launch post — Ferrynote 1.0'); counting only the post body, plain has 4 and 3.
Agents in both configs wrote scratch files to /tmp (pack more often: /tmp/crosscheck.py, /tmp/oldcheck/, /tmp/tdirrev/ and others). These were left in place.
